domain: Benefit compliance review (UK Universal Credit), manual casework with rule-based triage
intervention_type: triage rules + manual review programme; realized vs planned
source: National Audit Office, Tackling benefit overpayments due to fraud and error, HC 1336, Session 2024-2026 (Oct 2025), paras 3.18, 3.27-3.28, Figure 9
quote: Agents are allocated cases for review based on rules that are generated by using data and analytics to look for activity, behaviour or circumstances that suggest a higher risk of error. | Average productivity: the number of cases reviewed per agent per day was 1.07 in 2024-25, above DWP's expectation of 0.89. This was an improvement on the previous year when average productivity fell short of expectation. | Figure 9, 2023-24: average productivity expected 1.20, actual 0.57 | Cases completed: 1,151,000 cases were reviewed from 2022-23 to 2024-25, 104% of DWP's expectation of 1,104,000. | In 2024-25, the hit rate was 20%, which was less than the expectation of 24%. | DWP achieved an estimated £581 million in AME savings from TCR, 11% more than its expectation of £525 million
parameter: r_A (realized / planned throughput of a manual compliance process)
limitations: Throughput of a new manual review programme against its own plan, not labour saved by improving an existing process; triage rules are built with data analytics; outsourced agents; savings are benefit outcomes (AME), not admin cost; DWP management information analysed by NAO
model_use: A_FIELD lower bound 0.475 and upper bound 1.20; mode 1.0 with MI-E02

domain: Asylum casework (UK Home Office), eligibility decisions
intervention_type: process simplification (PACE: questionnaires, cohort rules, withdrawal rules), consultant-led; realized vs planned
source: National Audit Office, The asylum and protection transformation programme, HC 1375, Session 2022-23 (June 2023), Figure 9, paras 3.9, 3.12
quote: The Programme will increase caseworker weekly decisions from its July 2022 performance of 1.4 to 2.5. | established the Prioritising Asylum Customers' Experience (PACE) project to simplify decision-making and improve productivity. It engaged consultants, Newton, to support this work, on a contract worth £24 million. The Home Office hoped to increase productivity so each caseworker made an average of 2.5 decisions a week by the end of May 2023. In April 2023, the 640 active caseworkers (those making decisions) achieved the 2.5 decisions weekly. | 72% of decisions in April 2023 were 'administrative decisions' | The Infrastructure and Projects Authority (IPA) reported that there was an acknowledgement within the Home Office that publicly stated targets around productivity levels of caseworkers are not realistic.
parameter: r_A (realized / planned productivity gain of a non-technology process fix)
value: headline (2.5-1.4)/(2.5-1.4) = 1.00 among active caseworkers; planned gain 2.5/1.4 = 1.79x
limitations: Headline met largely through administrative decisions (withdrawals; 72% in April 2023), so labour per substantive decision is not measured; only ~50% of caseworkers were deciding claims; not finance; consultants' cost £24m
model_use: A_FIELD mode 1.0 (headline realization of the planned productivity)

domain: Complaint-review casework (UK Independent Office for Police Conduct)
intervention_type: workload balancing / self-organising allocation of cases; agency self-report
source: National Audit Office, Improving operational delivery in government: a good practice guide for senior leaders (March 2021), IOPC case; repeated in NAO, Efficiency in government, HC 303, Session 2021-22 (July 2021), Figure 7
quote: The leadership team experimented with giving casework teams ownership of how to manage their workload. | Total output has remained the same despite fewer people working in the team and spending more time on project work and additional responsibilities. IOPC says that productivity in one casework team may have increased by 33% compared with 12 months ago.
parameter: alpha (end-state labour saving per unit of output)
limitations: Self-report ('may have increased'), one team, no denominator or method; measured over the 12 months before March 2021 (edge of the 2021+ window); complaint review, not finance
model_use: Not used to set a range; consistent with v1 alpha upper bound 0.25

retrieved_via: econometricsociety.org abstract page (robots allowed); full text not read
quote: Exploiting the rotation of managers across sites, I find that a one standard deviation increase in managerial talent raises office productivity by 10%.
